Jennie starts with 60 letters needing stamps. She stamps one-third of them, which is \( \frac{1}{3} \times 60 = 20 \) letters. These 20 letters are moved to the already-stamped pile. After this, the already-stamped pile contains 30 letters. So, the initial number of already-stamped letters plus 20 equals 30. Therefore, the initial number was \( 30 - 20 = 10 \).

Answer: 10
